### 1.1 Purpose

This standard defines mandatory requirements for integrating Lenses.io with Okta Single Sign-On (SSO) using SAML 2.0, including Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) enforcement, group-based role mapping, and session management per [ADR-IFR-008](../../../decisions/infrastructure/ADR-IFR-008-kafka-management-platform-selection.md).
page_texts.6:
[standards/infrastructure/kafka-management/STD-INFRA-KMGMT-004-sso-integration.md#12-scope]

### 1.2 Scope

**In Scope**:
- Okta SAML 2.0 integration configuration
- MFA enforcement for all Lenses.io access
- SSO group-to-role mapping (SCIM provisioning)
- Session timeout and idle configuration
- Fallback local admin authentication
- Just-in-Time (JIT) user provisioning
- Logout flow and session cleanup

**Out of Scope**:
- Okta tenant configuration (managed by Identity team)
- RBAC role definitions (see STD-INFRA-KMGMT-003)
- Service account authentication (API keys, see STD-INFRA-KMGMT-003)
- AWS IAM authentication for MSK access (see STD-INFRA-INT-001)

#### REQ-LENS-004-001: Okta SAML 2.0 Integration

**Status**: Mandatory
**Rationale**: Centralized authentication via enterprise IDP

**Requirements**:
- Configure Lenses.io as SAML 2.0 Service Provider (SP)
- Register Lenses.io application in Okta with SAML 2.0 template
- Use ACS URL: `https://lenses.{environment}.company.com/api/saml/callback`
- Use Entity ID: `https://lenses.{environment}.company.com`
- Enable signed SAML assertions with SHA-256 signature algorithm
- Configure attribute mapping: email → NameID, groups → memberOf

**Implementation**:
```yaml
# Lenses.io SAML Configuration
# File: lenses-values.yaml (Helm chart)

lenses:
  security:
    mode: "SAML"

    saml:
      # Base URL for Lenses.io
      base.url: "https://lenses.${ENVIRONMENT}.company.com"

      # Okta SAML Identity Provider
      provider.url: "https://company.okta.com/app/${OKTA_APP_ID}/sso/saml"

      # SAML KeyStore Configuration
      keystore:
        location: "/mnt/secrets/saml-keystore.jks"
        password: ${SAML_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD}  # From Kubernetes secret
        alias: "lenses-saml"

      # IDP Metadata Configuration
      idp:
        metadata.url: "https://company.okta.com/app/${OKTA_APP_ID}/sso/saml/metadata"
        metadata.refresh.interval.minutes: 1440  # Refresh daily

      # Certificate and Signature Configuration
      signature:
        algorithm: "SHA256withRSA"
        validate.signature: true

      # Attribute Mapping from SAML Assertions
      attributes:
        username: "email"
        email: "email"
        firstName: "firstName"
        lastName: "lastName"
        groups: "memberOf"

      # NameID Configuration
      nameid:
        format: "urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress"

# Kubernetes Secret for SAML Keystore
# kubectl create secret generic lenses-saml-keystore \
#   --from-file=saml-keystore.jks \
#   --from-literal=password=${SAML_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD}
```

[standards/infrastructure/kafka-management/STD-INFRA-KMGMT-004-sso-integration.md#req-lens-004-002-mfa-enforcement]

#### REQ-LENS-004-002: MFA Enforcement

**Status**: Mandatory
**Rationale**: Defense-in-depth security per ADR-IFR-008

**Requirements**:
- Enforce MFA for **all** Lenses.io access (no exceptions)
- Configure Okta authentication policy requiring MFA
- Support Okta Verify, Google Authenticator, hardware tokens
- MFA challenge on every login (no remember device option)
- MFA re-authentication required after 12-hour idle session
- Block login attempts without MFA verification

**Okta Policy Configuration**:
1. Create Okta Sign-On Policy: "Lenses.io - MFA Required"
2. Rule: Require MFA for all users, all device types
3. Prompt for MFA: Every sign-on attempt
4. Session lifetime: 12 hours
5. Assign policy to Lenses.io SAML application

**Implementation**:
```hcl
# Okta Terraform Configuration
# File: okta-lenses-mfa-policy.tf

resource "okta_policy_signon" "lenses_mfa_required" {
  name        = "Lenses.io - MFA Required"
  status      = "ACTIVE"
  description = "Require MFA for all Lenses.io access"
  priority    = 1

  groups_included = [
    data.okta_group.lenses_platform_admins.id,
    data.okta_group.lenses_developers.id,
    data.okta_group.lenses_prod_developers.id,
    data.okta_group.lenses_read_only.id,
  ]
}

resource "okta_policy_rule_signon" "lenses_mfa_rule" {
  policy_id = okta_policy_signon.lenses_mfa_required.id
  name      = "Require MFA - All Users"
  status    = "ACTIVE"
  priority  = 1

  # Require MFA for all users
  mfa_required    = true
  mfa_prompt      = "ALWAYS"  # Prompt on every login
  mfa_remember_device = false # Never remember device

  # Session configuration
  session_idle         = 120   # 2 hours idle timeout
  session_lifetime     = 720   # 12 hours absolute
  session_persistent   = false # Don't persist across browser restarts

  # Apply to all users, all device types, all network locations
  network_connection = "ANYWHERE"
}

# Assign policy to Lenses.io SAML application
resource "okta_app_signon_policy_rule" "lenses_saml" {
  policy_id = okta_policy_signon.lenses_mfa_required.id
  app_include = [okta_app_saml.lenses.id]
}
```

[standards/infrastructure/kafka-management/STD-INFRA-KMGMT-004-sso-integration.md#req-lens-004-003-group-based-role-mapping]

#### REQ-LENS-004-003: Group-Based Role Mapping

**Status**: Mandatory
**Rationale**: Automated access control via SSO groups

**Requirements**:
- Map Okta groups to Lenses.io roles (defined in STD-INFRA-KMGMT-003)
- Use SAML attribute "memberOf" to pass group memberships
- Configure group-to-role mappings in Lenses.io:
  - `okta_lenses_platform_admins` → Platform Admin role
  - `okta_lenses_developers_{business-unit}` → Developer role (scoped to BU)
  - `okta_lenses_prod_developers` → Production Developer role
  - `okta_lenses_read_only` → Read-Only role
- Apply role assignments on every login (dynamic group membership)
- Support multiple group memberships (highest privilege wins)

**Implementation**:
```yaml
# Group-to-Role Mapping Configuration
# File: lenses-values.yaml (Helm chart)

lenses:
  security:
    saml:
      groups:
        # SAML attribute containing group memberships
        attribute: "memberOf"

        # Mapping rules (evaluated in order, first match wins)
        mappings:
          # Platform Administrators (highest privilege)
          - group: "okta_lenses_platform_admins"
            role: "PlatformAdmin"
            description: "Full administrative access to Lenses.io"

          # Production Developers (time-limited production access)
          - group: "okta_lenses_prod_developers"
            role: "ProductionDeveloper"
            description: "Temporary production access with approval"

          # Developers by Business Unit (scoped access)
          - group: "okta_lenses_developers_claims"
            role: "Developer"
            scope:
              topics: "claims.*"
              consumerGroups: "claims-*"
            description: "Claims business unit developer access"

          - group: "okta_lenses_developers_enrollment"
            role: "Developer"
            scope:
              topics: "enrollment.*"
              consumerGroups: "enrollment-*"
            description: "Enrollment business unit developer access"

          - group: "okta_lenses_developers_pharmacy"
            role: "Developer"
            scope:
              topics: "pharmacy.*"
              consumerGroups: "pharmacy-*"
            description: "Pharmacy business unit developer access"

          - group: "okta_lenses_developers_provider"
            role: "Developer"
            scope:
              topics: "provider.*"
              consumerGroups: "provider-*"
            description: "Provider business unit developer access"

          - group: "okta_lenses_developers_analytics"
            role: "Developer"
            scope:
              topics: "analytics.*"
              consumerGroups: "analytics-*"
            description: "Analytics business unit developer access"

          # Data Stewards (schema governance)
          - group: "okta_lenses_data_stewards"
            role: "DataSteward"
            description: "Schema registry and data governance access"

          # Read-Only Users (lowest privilege)
          - group: "okta_lenses_read_only"
            role: "ReadOnly"
            description: "View-only access to all clusters"

        # Role precedence rules (if user in multiple groups)
        precedence:
          - "PlatformAdmin"      # Highest
          - "DataSteward"
          - "ProductionDeveloper"
          - "Developer"
          - "ReadOnly"            # Lowest

        # Default role if no group matches (deny access)
        default.role: null  # No default role - must be in at least one group
```

[standards/infrastructure/kafka-management/STD-INFRA-KMGMT-004-sso-integration.md#req-lens-004-004-just-in-time-jit-user-provisioning]

#### REQ-LENS-004-004: Just-in-Time (JIT) User Provisioning

**Status**: Mandatory
**Rationale**: Automated user lifecycle management

**Requirements**:
- Enable JIT provisioning to auto-create users on first login
- Populate user attributes from SAML assertions:
  - Username: email address
  - Display name: firstName + lastName
  - Email: email
  - Groups: memberOf
- Assign roles based on group membership (REQ-LENS-004-003)
- Do NOT pre-provision users manually (except local admin)
- Deactivate users in Lenses.io when removed from all Okta groups (via SCIM if available)

**Implementation**:
```yaml
# Just-in-Time (JIT) User Provisioning Configuration
# File: lenses-values.yaml (Helm chart)

lenses:
  security:
    saml:
      jit:
        # Enable JIT user provisioning
        enabled: true

        # User creation on first login
        create.user.on.login: true

        # User attribute mapping from SAML assertions
        user.attributes:
          username: "{email}"  # Use email as username
          displayName: "{firstName} {lastName}"
          email: "{email}"
          groups: "{memberOf}"  # Dynamic group membership

        # User lifecycle management
        user.lifecycle:
          # Update user attributes on every login
          update.on.login: true

          # Deactivate users when removed from all Okta groups
          deactivate.on.no.groups: true

          # Grace period before deactivation (hours)
          deactivation.grace.period: 24

          # Archive inactive users after 90 days
          archive.after.days: 90

        # Role assignment behavior
        role.assignment:
          # Update roles on every login (dynamic)
          dynamic: true

          # Allow multiple roles if user in multiple groups
          allow.multiple: false  # Highest precedence role only

          # Deny access if no role assigned
          deny.if.no.role: true

        # Audit configuration
        audit:
          # Log all JIT provisioning events
          log.user.creation: true
          log.user.updates: true
          log.user.deactivation: true

          # CloudWatch log group for JIT events
          cloudwatch.log.group: "/aws/lenses/${ENVIRONMENT}/jit-provisioning"
```

[standards/infrastructure/kafka-management/STD-INFRA-KMGMT-004-sso-integration.md#req-lens-004-005-session-management]

#### REQ-LENS-004-005: Session Management

**Status**: Mandatory
**Rationale**: Limit exposure window for compromised sessions

**Requirements**:
- Session timeout: 12 hours absolute (Okta policy)
- Idle timeout: 2 hours (Lenses.io configuration)
- Force re-authentication after idle timeout (redirect to Okta login)
- Invalidate session on logout (Okta + Lenses.io)
- Support Okta Single Logout (SLO) - logout from Okta logs out from Lenses.io
- Clear browser cookies on logout

**Implementation**:
```yaml
# Session Management Configuration
# File: lenses-values.yaml (Helm chart)

lenses:
  security:
    session:
      # Session timeouts
      max.lifetime.minutes: 720   # 12 hours absolute (matches Okta)
      idle.timeout.minutes: 120    # 2 hours idle timeout

      # Session invalidation
      invalidate.on.logout: true
      invalidate.on.role.change: true

      # Session storage
      storage:
        type: "redis"  # Use Redis for distributed session storage
        redis:
          host: "lenses-redis.${NAMESPACE}.svc.cluster.local"
          port: 6379
          database: 0
          password: ${REDIS_PASSWORD}  # From Kubernetes secret
          timeout.seconds: 5

      # Cookie configuration
      cookie:
        name: "LENSES_SESSION"
        secure: true      # HTTPS only
        httpOnly: true    # No JavaScript access
        sameSite: "Lax"   # CSRF protection
        domain: ".company.com"
        path: "/"

    saml:
      # Single Logout (SLO) Configuration
      logout:
        enabled: true

        # Okta logout URL
        url: "https://company.okta.com/login/signout"

        # Logout response URL (where Okta redirects after logout)
        response.url: "https://lenses.${ENVIRONMENT}.company.com/logout/callback"

        # Single Logout Request (SP-initiated)
        slo.request:
          enabled: true
          binding: "urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:bindings:HTTP-Redirect"

        # Single Logout Response (IDP-initiated)
        slo.response:
          enabled: true
          binding: "urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:bindings:HTTP-Redirect"

        # Cleanup actions on logout
        cleanup:
          clear.cookies: true
          invalidate.session: true
          revoke.tokens: true

# Redis deployment for session storage
# Configured via separate Helm chart: bitnami/redis
redis:
  auth:
    enabled: true
    password: ${REDIS_PASSWORD}
  master:
    persistence:
      enabled: true
      size: 8Gi
  replica:
    replicaCount: 2
  metrics:
    enabled: true
```

[standards/infrastructure/kafka-management/STD-INFRA-KMGMT-004-sso-integration.md#req-lens-004-006-fallback-local-authentication]

#### REQ-LENS-004-006: Fallback Local Authentication

**Status**: Mandatory
**Rationale**: Emergency access when Okta unavailable

**Requirements**:
- Maintain **one** local admin account: `lenses-admin-emergency`
- Store credentials in AWS Secrets Manager with restricted access
- Rotate local admin password every 90 days
- Audit all local admin login attempts (CloudWatch alert on login)
- Disable local admin account unless required for emergency
- Enable local admin only during Okta outage (manual process)

**Emergency Access Procedure**:
1. Verify Okta outage (Okta status page, 30+ minute downtime)
2. Platform Engineering Director approves emergency access
3. Retrieve credentials from AWS Secrets Manager
4. Enable local authentication in Lenses.io configuration
5. Restart Lenses.io pods to apply configuration
6. Login with local admin credentials
7. After Okta recovery: Disable local auth, restart pods, rotate password

**Implementation**:
```yaml
# Local Authentication Configuration (Emergency Access Only)
# File: lenses-values-emergency.yaml (separate file, not deployed by default)

lenses:
  security:
    # Enable BOTH SAML and local auth during emergency
    mode: "SAML"

    # Local users (disabled by default)
    local:
      enabled: false  # Set to true only during Okta outage

      users:
        - username: "lenses-admin-emergency"
          password: ${LOCAL_ADMIN_PASSWORD}  # From AWS Secrets Manager
          roles:
            - "PlatformAdmin"
          metadata:
            created: "2026-01-20"
            purpose: "Emergency access during Okta outage"
            rotation.days: 90

# AWS Secrets Manager integration for local admin password
# Secret name: lenses/${ENVIRONMENT}/emergency-admin-password
# Rotation: Lambda function rotates every 90 days

---
# Emergency Access Procedure Script
# File: scripts/enable-emergency-access.sh

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

ENVIRONMENT=$1
NAMESPACE="lenses-${ENVIRONMENT}"

echo "⚠️  EMERGENCY ACCESS ACTIVATION for ${ENVIRONMENT}"
echo "This should ONLY be used during Okta outage"
read -p "Have you verified Okta is down? (yes/no): " CONFIRM

if [ "$CONFIRM" != "yes" ]; then
  echo "Aborted."
  exit 1
fi

# 1. Retrieve local admin password from AWS Secrets Manager
echo "1. Retrieving emergency admin password..."
LOCAL_ADMIN_PASSWORD=$(aws secretsmanager get-secret-value \
  --secret-id "lenses/${ENVIRONMENT}/emergency-admin-password" \
  --query 'SecretString' \
  --output text | jq -r '.password')

# 2. Create Kubernetes secret with local admin credentials
echo "2. Creating emergency access secret..."
kubectl create secret generic lenses-emergency-auth \
  --from-literal=local-admin-password="${LOCAL_ADMIN_PASSWORD}" \
  --namespace="${NAMESPACE}" \
  --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -

# 3. Update Lenses Helm release to enable local auth
echo "3. Enabling local authentication in Lenses.io..."
helm upgrade lenses lenses/lenses \
  --namespace="${NAMESPACE}" \
  --reuse-values \
  --set lenses.security.local.enabled=true \
  --set lenses.security.local.users[0].password="${LOCAL_ADMIN_PASSWORD}"

# 4. Wait for pods to restart
echo "4. Waiting for Lenses pods to restart..."
kubectl rollout status deployment/lenses -n "${NAMESPACE}" --timeout=5m

echo ""
echo "✅ Emergency access ENABLED"
echo "Username: lenses-admin-emergency"
echo "Password: (retrieved from AWS Secrets Manager)"
echo ""
echo "⚠️  REMEMBER TO DISABLE after Okta recovery:"
echo "   ./scripts/disable-emergency-access.sh ${ENVIRONMENT}"
echo ""

# 5. Send CloudWatch alert
aws cloudwatch put-metric-data \
  --namespace "Lenses/Security" \
  --metric-name "EmergencyAccessEnabled" \
  --value 1 \
  --dimensions Environment="${ENVIRONMENT}"

# 6. Create incident ticket
echo "6. Creating incident ticket in ServiceNow..."
# (Placeholder for ServiceNow API call)
```

[standards/infrastructure/kafka-management/STD-INFRA-KMGMT-004-sso-integration.md#req-lens-004-008-certificate-management]

#### REQ-LENS-004-008: Certificate Management

**Status**: Mandatory
**Rationale**: Secure SAML assertion signing and encryption

**Requirements**:
- Generate X.509 certificate for SAML signing (2048-bit RSA minimum)
- Store certificate in Kubernetes secret: `lenses-saml-keystore`
- Certificate validity: 2 years
- Renew certificate 30 days before expiration
- Upload certificate to Okta SAML app (Service Provider certificate)
- Monitor certificate expiration via CloudWatch alarm (30-day warning)

**Certificate Generation**:
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# SAML Certificate Generation and Management Script
# File: scripts/generate-saml-certificate.sh

set -euo pipefail

ENVIRONMENT=$1
NAMESPACE="lenses-${ENVIRONMENT}"
CERT_VALIDITY_DAYS=730  # 2 years

echo "Generating SAML certificate for Lenses.io (${ENVIRONMENT})..."

# 1. Generate private key (2048-bit RSA)
echo "1. Generating RSA private key..."
openssl genrsa -out lenses-saml-private.key 2048

# 2. Generate certificate signing request (CSR)
echo "2. Creating certificate signing request..."
openssl req -new -key lenses-saml-private.key -out lenses-saml.csr -subj "/C=US/ST=State/L=City/O=Company/OU=Platform Engineering/CN=lenses.${ENVIRONMENT}.company.com"

# 3. Generate self-signed certificate (valid for 2 years)
echo "3. Generating self-signed certificate..."
openssl x509 -req -days "${CERT_VALIDITY_DAYS}" \
  -in lenses-saml.csr \
  -signkey lenses-saml-private.key \
  -out lenses-saml-certificate.crt \
  -sha256

# 4. Create PKCS12 keystore
echo "4. Creating PKCS12 keystore..."
KEYSTORE_PASSWORD=$(openssl rand -base64 32)
openssl pkcs12 -export \
  -in lenses-saml-certificate.crt \
  -inkey lenses-saml-private.key \
  -out lenses-saml.p12 \
  -name "lenses-saml" \
  -passout pass:"${KEYSTORE_PASSWORD}"

# 5. Convert to JKS format (required by Lenses.io)
echo "5. Converting to JKS keystore..."
keytool -importkeystore \
  -srckeystore lenses-saml.p12 \
  -srcstoretype PKCS12 \
  -srcstorepass "${KEYSTORE_PASSWORD}" \
  -destkeystore lenses-saml-keystore.jks \
  -deststoretype JKS \
  -deststorepass "${KEYSTORE_PASSWORD}" \
  -destkeypass "${KEYSTORE_PASSWORD}" \
  -alias "lenses-saml"

# 6. Create Kubernetes secret with keystore
echo "6. Creating Kubernetes secret..."
kubectl create secret generic lenses-saml-keystore \
  --from-file=saml-keystore.jks=lenses-saml-keystore.jks \
  --from-literal=keystore-password="${KEYSTORE_PASSWORD}" \
  --namespace="${NAMESPACE}" \
  --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -

# 7. Store certificate in AWS Secrets Manager for backup
echo "7. Storing certificate in AWS Secrets Manager..."
aws secretsmanager create-secret \
  --name "lenses/${ENVIRONMENT}/saml-certificate" \
  --description "SAML certificate for Lenses.io (${ENVIRONMENT})" \
  --secret-string "$(cat <<EOF
{
  "certificate": "$(base64 -w 0 lenses-saml-certificate.crt)",
  "private_key": "$(base64 -w 0 lenses-saml-private.key)",
  "keystore_password": "${KEYSTORE_PASSWORD}",
  "created_date": "$(date -I)",
  "expiration_date": "$(date -d "+${CERT_VALIDITY_DAYS} days" -I)"
}
EOF
)" || aws secretsmanager update-secret \
  --secret-id "lenses/${ENVIRONMENT}/saml-certificate" \
  --secret-string "$(cat <<EOF
{
  "certificate": "$(base64 -w 0 lenses-saml-certificate.crt)",
  "private_key": "$(base64 -w 0 lenses-saml-private.key)",
  "keystore_password": "${KEYSTORE_PASSWORD}",
  "created_date": "$(date -I)",
  "expiration_date": "$(date -d "+${CERT_VALIDITY_DAYS} days" -I)"
}
EOF
)"

# 8. Upload certificate to Okta SAML app
echo "8. Uploading certificate to Okta..."
echo "   Manual step: Navigate to Okta Admin Console"
echo "   1. Applications → Lenses.io - ${ENVIRONMENT}"
echo "   2. Sign On tab → SAML 2.0 → Edit"
echo "   3. Service Provider Certificate → Upload: lenses-saml-certificate.crt"
echo "   4. Save"
echo ""
echo "Certificate file: lenses-saml-certificate.crt"
cat lenses-saml-certificate.crt
echo ""

# 9. Set up certificate expiration monitoring
echo "9. Creating certificate expiration CloudWatch alarm..."
EXPIRATION_TIMESTAMP=$(date -d "+${CERT_VALIDITY_DAYS} days" +%s)
aws cloudwatch put-metric-alarm \
  --alarm-name "Lenses-SAML-Certificate-Expiration-${ENVIRONMENT}" \
  --alarm-description "SAML certificate expires in 30 days" \
  --metric-name "CertificateExpirationDays" \
  --namespace "Lenses/Security" \
  --statistic "Minimum" \
  --period 86400 \
  --evaluation-periods 1 \
  --threshold 30 \
  --comparison-operator "LessThanThreshold" \
  --alarm-actions "arn:aws:sns:us-east-1:123456789012:lenses-alerts" \
  --dimensions Name=Environment,Value="${ENVIRONMENT}" Name=CertificateType,Value=SAML

# 10. Clean up temporary files
echo "10. Cleaning up temporary files..."
rm -f lenses-saml.csr lenses-saml.p12

echo ""
```

#### REQ-LENS-004-009: SSO Validation and Testing

**Status**: Mandatory
**Rationale**: Verify SSO integration before production use

**Test Cases**:
1. **Successful Login**: User in `okta_lenses_developers` logs in, assigned Developer role
2. **MFA Enforcement**: Login blocked without MFA verification
3. **Group Mapping**: User added to `okta_lenses_platform_admins` immediately gets Platform Admin role
4. **Session Timeout**: Session expires after 2 hours idle, user redirected to Okta login
5. **Single Logout**: Logout from Lenses.io logs out from Okta (and all other Okta apps)
6. **JIT Provisioning**: New user auto-created on first login with correct role
7. **Fallback Auth**: Local admin account works when SAML disabled (emergency only)
8. **Attribute Mapping**: User profile displays correct email, firstName, lastName

```python
OKTA_PASSWORD = os.getenv('OKTA_TEST_PASSWORD')

        """Initialize Chrome WebDriver"""

        options.add_argument('--no-sandbox')

        """Test Case 1: User successfully logs in with MFA"""
        print("\nTest 1: Successful Login with MFA")

        # 1. Navigate to Lenses.io
        driver.get(LENSES_BASE_URL)

        # 2. Should redirect to Okta login
        WebDriverWait(driver, 10).until(
            EC.presence_of_element_located((By.ID, "okta-signin-username"))
        )
        assert "okta.com" in driver.current_url

        # 3. Enter credentials
        driver.find_element(By.ID, "okta-signin-username").send_keys(OKTA_USERNAME)
        driver.find_element(By.ID, "okta-signin-password").send_keys(OKTA_PASSWORD)

    def test_03_group_role_mapping(self, driver):
        """Test Case 3: User assigned correct role based on group membership"""
        print("\nTest 3: Group-to-Role Mapping")

        # Prerequisites: Test user must be in okta_lenses_developers_claims group
```

#### REQ-LENS-004-010: SSO Audit and Monitoring

**Status**: Mandatory
**Rationale**: Detect authentication anomalies and SSO failures

**Monitored Metrics**:
- Failed SSO login attempts (alert if >10/hour)
- Successful login rate (alert if <80% success rate)
- SAML assertion validation failures (alert on any occurrence)
- Local admin login attempts (alert immediately)
- Session timeout events (track for capacity planning)
- Group membership changes (log for audit)

**CloudWatch Alarms**:
- `LensesSSO-FailedLoginRate` (threshold: 10 failures/hour)
- `LensesSSO-LocalAdminLogin` (threshold: any occurrence)
- `LensesSSO-SAMLAssertionError` (threshold: any occurrence)

**Implementation**:
```yaml
# SSO Monitoring and Alerting Configuration
# File: cloudwatch/lenses-sso-monitoring.yaml

apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: lenses-sso-monitoring
  namespace: lenses-${ENVIRONMENT}
data:
  # CloudWatch Log Filters for SSO Events
  log-filters.json: |
    [
      {
        "filterName": "LensesSSO-FailedLoginAttempts",
        "filterPattern": "[timestamp, request_id, level=ERROR, logger=*SAML*, message=*authentication*failed*]",
        "metricTransformations": [
          {
            "metricName": "FailedSAMLLogin",
            "metricNamespace": "Lenses/SSO",
            "metricValue": "1",
            "defaultValue": 0,
            "dimensions": {
              "Environment": "${ENVIRONMENT}",
              "Component": "SAML"
            }
          }
        ]
      },
      {
        "filterName": "LensesSSO-SuccessfulLoginRate",
        "filterPattern": "[timestamp, request_id, level=INFO, logger=*SAML*, message=*authentication*successful*]",
        "metricTransformations": [
          {
            "metricName": "SuccessfulSAMLLogin",
            "metricNamespace": "Lenses/SSO",
            "metricValue": "1",
            "defaultValue": 0
          }
        ]
      },
      {
        "filterName": "LensesSSO-SAMLAssertionErrors",
        "filterPattern": "[timestamp, request_id, level=ERROR, logger=*SAML*, message=*assertion*invalid* || message=*signature*failed*]",
        "metricTransformations": [
          {
            "metricName": "SAMLAssertionError",
            "metricNamespace": "Lenses/SSO",
            "metricValue": "1",
            "defaultValue": 0
          }
        ]
      },
      {
        "filterName": "LensesSSO-LocalAdminLogin",
        "filterPattern": "[timestamp, request_id, level=INFO, logger=*Auth*, message=*local*admin*login*]",
        "metricTransformations": [
          {
            "metricName": "LocalAdminLogin",
            "metricNamespace": "Lenses/SSO",
            "metricValue": "1",
            "defaultValue": 0
          }
        ]
      },
      {
        "filterName": "LensesSSO-SessionTimeouts",
        "filterPattern": "[timestamp, request_id, level=INFO, logger=*Session*, message=*timeout* || message=*expired*]",
        "metricTransformations": [
          {
            "metricName": "SessionTimeout",
            "metricNamespace": "Lenses/SSO",
            "metricValue": "1",
            "defaultValue": 0
          }
        ]
      },
      {
        "filterName": "LensesSSO-GroupMembershipChanges",
        "filterPattern": "[timestamp, request_id, level=INFO, logger=*SAML*, message=*group*membership*changed*]",
        "metricTransformations": [
          {
            "metricName": "GroupMembershipChange",
            "metricNamespace": "Lenses/SSO",
            "metricValue": "1",
            "defaultValue": 0
          }
        ]
      }
    ]

---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: lenses-sso-alarms
  namespace: lenses-${ENVIRONMENT}
data:
  # CloudWatch Alarms for SSO Monitoring
  alarms.json: |
    [
      {
        "AlarmName": "LensesSSO-FailedLoginRate-${ENVIRONMENT}",

          }
        ],
        "AlarmActions": [
          "arn:aws:sns:us-east-1:123456789012:lenses-security-alerts"
        ],
        "TreatMissingData": "notBreaching"
      },
      {
        "AlarmName": "LensesSSO-LocalAdminLogin-${ENVIRONMENT}",
        "AlarmDescription": "IMMEDIATE ALERT: Local admin account used (emergency access)",
        "MetricName": "LocalAdminLogin",
        "Namespace": "Lenses/SSO",
        "Statistic": "Sum",
        "Period": 60,
        "EvaluationPeriods": 1,
        "Threshold": 0,
        "ComparisonOperator": "GreaterThanThreshold",
        "AlarmActions": [
          "arn:aws:sns:us-east-1:123456789012:lenses-critical-alerts"
        ],
        "TreatMissingData": "notBreaching"
      },
      {
        "AlarmName": "LensesSSO-SAMLAssertionError-${ENVIRONMENT}",
        "AlarmDescription": "SAML assertion validation failures detected",
        "MetricName": "SAMLAssertionError",
        "Namespace": "Lenses/SSO",
        "Statistic": "Sum",
        "Period": 300,
        "EvaluationPeriods": 1,
        "Threshold": 0,
        "ComparisonOperator": "GreaterThanThreshold",
        "AlarmActions": [
          "arn:aws:sns:us-east-1:123456789012:lenses-security-alerts"
        ],
        "TreatMissingData": "notBreaching"
      },
      {
        "AlarmName": "LensesSSO-LowSuccessRate-${ENVIRONMENT}",
        "AlarmDescription": "SSO login success rate below 80%",
        "Metrics": [
          {
            "Id": "m1",
            "MetricStat": {
              "Metric": {
                "Namespace": "Lenses/SSO",
                "MetricName": "SuccessfulSAMLLogin"
              },
              "Period": 3600,
              "Stat": "Sum"
            }
          },
          {
            "Id": "m2",
            "MetricStat": {
              "Metric": {
                "Namespace": "Lenses/SSO",

              },
              "Period": 3600,
              "Stat": "Sum"

          },
          {
            "Id": "e1",
            "Expression": "m1 / (m1 + m2) * 100",

        "EvaluationPeriods": 2,

        "ComparisonOperator": "LessThanThreshold",
```

#### Issue 1: SAML Assertion Signature Verification Failure

**Symptoms**: Error message "Invalid SAML assertion signature"

**Resolution**:
1. Verify Okta certificate uploaded to Lenses.io matches Okta metadata
2. Check SAML assertion signature algorithm (must be SHA-256)
3. Ensure Lenses.io keystore password is correct
4. Restart Lenses.io pods to reload certificate

#### Issue 2: Group Membership Not Mapped to Roles

**Symptoms**: User logs in but has no roles/access denied

**Resolution**:
1. Verify Okta sends "memberOf" attribute in SAML assertion (check SAML tracer)
2. Confirm user is member of at least one Lenses.io Okta group
3. Check group-to-role mapping configuration in Lenses.io
4. Ensure group name matches exactly (case-sensitive)
5. Test with Read-Only role assignment (lowest privilege)

**Resolution**:
1. Verify session configuration in Lenses.io Helm values
2. Check browser cookies (should have `Max-Age` header)
3. Confirm Okta session lifetime matches Lenses.io configuration

### 4.3 Monitoring Requirements

**Continuous Monitoring**:

- **Authentication Patterns**: Monitor for unusual login patterns or repeated failures
- **MFA Bypass Attempts**: Alert on any attempts to bypass MFA requirements
- **SAML Errors**: Track SAML assertion validation failures and signature errors
- **Session Anomalies**: Detect abnormal session duration or concurrent sessions
- **Certificate Health**: Monitor SAML certificate expiration and validity
- **Emergency Access**: Immediate alerts on local admin account usage

**Periodic Reviews**:

- **Daily**: SSO success rate, MFA compliance, certificate validity
- **Weekly**: Group membership sync, role assignment accuracy
- **Monthly**: Emergency access audit, Okta policy review
- **Quarterly**: SSO integration security assessment, penetration testing

**Incident Reporting**:

- **Immediate**: Local admin login, SAML certificate expiration, MFA bypass attempts
- **Hourly**: SSO success rate below 95%, repeated SAML assertion failures
- **Daily**: Group-to-role mapping errors, session timeout violations
- **Weekly**: Cumulative failed authentication trends

[standards/infrastructure/kafka-management/STD-INFRA-KMGMT-004-sso-integration.md#44-exception-handling]

### 4.4 Exception Handling

**Exception Categories**:

1. **Temporary MFA Exemption** (Generally Prohibited):
   - **Justification Required**: Critical business need (extremely rare)
   - **Approval**: CISO + Security Director + Platform Engineering Director
   - **Duration**: Maximum 24 hours, non-renewable
   - **Monitoring**: Enhanced logging, dedicated CloudWatch alert
   - **Alternative**: Use emergency local admin access instead

2. **Extended Session Timeout**:
   - **Justification Required**: Long-running operations or batch processing needs
   - **Approval**: Manager + Security Team review
   - **Duration**: Maximum 24 hours (vs standard 12 hours)
   - **Monitoring**: Session activity logging
   - **Review**: Monthly validation of necessity

3. **Additional Local Admin Accounts**:
   - **Justification Required**: Multi-region disaster recovery requirement
   - **Approval**: Architecture Review Board + CISO
   - **Implementation**: Per-region emergency accounts only
   - **Monitoring**: Same audit requirements as primary account
   - **Review**: Quarterly necessity validation

4. **Custom SAML Attribute Mapping**:
   - **Justification Required**: Special organizational structure
   - **Approval**: Identity Team + Platform Engineering Lead
   - **Documentation**: Detailed attribute mapping documentation
   - **Testing**: Comprehensive SSO test suite validation
   - **Review**: Annual effectiveness review

**Exception Management Process**:

1. Submit via ServiceNow with detailed justification and risk assessment
2. Security team reviews security implications and alternative solutions
3. Approval workflow routes to appropriate approvers based on exception type
4. Implementation with enhanced monitoring and documentation
5. Quarterly review of all active exceptions
6. Auto-expiration and remediation planning

### 4.5 Governance Oversight

**Standards Owner**: Director of Platform Engineering
- Responsible for maintaining and updating this SSO integration standard
- Reviews quarterly for continued relevance and accuracy
- Coordinates with Identity and Security teams on changes
- Publishes updates and communicates to stakeholders

**Compliance Manager**: Security Operations Manager
- Monitors organizational SSO compliance metrics
- Manages exception requests and tracking
- Reports compliance status to governance bodies
- Coordinates remediation of policy violations

**Technical Stewards**:
- **Identity Team**: Okta configuration, MFA policies, group management
- **Platform Engineering**: Lenses.io SAML configuration, certificate management
- **Security Team**: Security policy enforcement, audit review, threat monitoring

**Governance Bodies**:
- **Security Council**: Approves MFA policy changes and security exceptions
- **Architecture Review Board**: Reviews custom SAML configurations
- **Change Advisory Board**: Approves production SSO configuration changes
